name: Trichophytic closure
summary: A suturing method that lets hair grow through the donor scar after strip harvesting; evidence is small comparative studies.
lead: Trichophytic closure is a wound-closure technique used after strip (FUT) donor harvesting in hair transplantation and in facelift incisions. Wound edges are prepared so hair can grow through the scar, helping camouflage it.

name: Platelet-rich fibrin for hair
summary: A blood-derived fibrin clot used in dentistry and tried off-label for hair thinning, with almost no hair-specific research.
lead: Platelet-rich fibrin (PRF) is a preparation made from a person's own blood that concentrates platelets and white blood cells in a fibrin matrix. It is described as a derivative of platelet-rich plasma (PRP) and is documented mainly as a tissue-engineering scaffold in oral and maxillofacial surgery . Its use for hair restoration is a newer, off-label application discussed in aesthetic medicine.

name: Hair micropigmentation
summary: A scalp tattoo that mimics a buzz cut or camouflages scars; long-lasting, but backed by press coverage rather than studies.
lead: Hair micropigmentation, usually called scalp micropigmentation (SMP) or a hair tattoo, is a non-surgical cosmetic tattoo applied to the scalp. It is used to create the look of a closely shaved head on a bald scalp, to add apparent density to a thinning crown, or to conceal hair-transplant scars and other scars on the head .

name: Eyelash implants
summary: Surgical placement of hair into the eyelids for fuller lashes; sources reviewed give only history, no outcome studies.
lead: Eyelash implants, also called eyelash transplantation, refer to surgical procedures that place hair into the eyelid margin to create or thicken lashes. They differ from temporary eyelash extensions or false lashes, which are applied to or alongside existing lashes.

name: Artificial hair integrations
summary: Extensions, weaves and mesh systems that add hair over thinning areas; reversible, but traction and adhesive problems are documented.
lead: Artificial hair integrations are prosthetic hair products, such as extensions, weaves, hairpieces and mesh-based integration systems, that add length, volume or coverage to a person's own hair using human or synthetic fibre. They are used for styling and to camouflage hair loss from conditions such as alopecia .

name: Scalp cooling cap
summary: A cap that chills the scalp during chemotherapy to reduce hair loss; studied mainly in breast cancer patients, with trial support for that use.
lead: A scalp cooling cap is a tight-fitting cap that lowers scalp temperature during chemotherapy, with the aim of reducing chemotherapy-induced hair loss. Caps are either manual gel or ice caps that are frozen beforehand and swapped during treatment, or machine-based systems in which a control unit keeps coolant circulating .

name: Intralesional corticosteroid scalp injection
summary: Steroid injected into patchy hair-loss spots, mainly alopecia areata; reported regrowth is high but spontaneous remission complicates it.
lead: Intralesional corticosteroid injection places a corticosteroid, most often triamcinolone, directly into patches of hair loss. Wikipedia's article on alopecia areata says steroid injections are commonly used where the hair loss areas on the head are small or where eyebrow hair has been lost .

name: In-office laser whitening
summary: Peroxide gel on the teeth with a light or laser to speed it up; whether the light adds anything beyond the gel is still contested.
lead: In-office laser whitening is a professional tooth-bleaching procedure in which a peroxide gel is applied to the teeth and a light source, described by providers as a laser, LED or diode unit, is directed at it to accelerate the colour change. It is delivered by dental staff, with the gums protected by a barrier, and is one of several light-activated in-office options.

name: Zoom whitening
summary: A branded dentist-applied peroxide-and-light whitening session; shade change is typical, sensitivity common.
lead: Zoom whitening is the name commonly given to a branded, light-activated in-office tooth-whitening treatment in which a high-strength hydrogen peroxide gel is applied by dental staff and exposed to a lamp. It belongs to the wider category of in-office power bleaching described on Wikipedia, which uses roughly 25-38% hydrogen peroxide with 6-15 minutes of light exposure.

name: Gum depigmentation
summary: Dentist-performed lightening of dark gums by scalpel, laser or chemicals, backed so far by small comparison trials.
lead: Gum depigmentation is a cosmetic periodontal procedure that lightens dark (melanin-pigmented) gums, using a scalpel, laser or chemical methods. Wikipedia notes that gum pigmentation is mainly linked to genetics and tobacco smoking (smoker's melanosis), with melanin made by melanocytes in the gum's basal layer.

name: Enameloplasty (tooth reshaping)
summary: Dentist shaves tiny amounts of enamel to alter tooth shape; permanent, and no appearance studies were found.
lead: Enameloplasty, also called tooth reshaping or contouring, is the removal of small amounts of enamel to change a tooth's length, shape or surface, for example to smooth a chip or even out an edge. Wikipedia's cosmetic-dentistry article says it gives fast results and can sometimes stand in for braces, but that removed enamel is irreplaceable and dentin may be exposed.

name: Porcelain veneers
summary: Thin ceramic shells bonded to the front of teeth; long-lasting in follow-up studies but they usually require irreversible enamel removal.
lead: Porcelain veneers are thin, custom-made shells, usually of porcelain or glass-ceramic, bonded to the front of teeth to change their colour, shape, size or spacing. They are made indirectly by a dental technician, unlike composite veneers, which can be built directly in the mouth.

name: Maryland bridge
summary: A winged bridge glued to neighbouring teeth to replace a missing tooth with little drilling; debonding is the usual failure.
lead: A Maryland bridge, also called a resin-bonded or adhesive bridge, replaces a missing tooth with a pontic that has metal or ceramic 'wings' bonded to the etched enamel of neighbouring teeth, requiring little or no preparation of them. Its name is noted on Wikipedia, which has no history section for it.

name: Gum graft
summary: Surgery that moves gum tissue over exposed roots; used for recession and sometimes for looks, with donor-site pain the main reported downside.
lead: A gum graft, also called gingival grafting or periodontal plastic surgery, is a family of surgical procedures in which gum tissue is moved or added to cover exposed tooth roots or to thicken a thin band of gum . It is most often performed by periodontists, and the usual reason is gum recession, in which the gum margin has migrated away from the crown and exposed the root surface .

name: Gum lift
summary: Reshaping the gumline, sometimes with bone, to show more tooth; evidence for cosmetic use is thin and bone removal is permanent.
lead: A gum lift is the cosmetic term for reshaping the gumline to expose more of the tooth, a procedure that overlaps with crown lengthening . Crown lengthening is a surgical procedure, usually performed by a periodontist, that exposes more tooth by removing some gum tissue and sometimes supporting bone .

name: Internal bleaching
summary: Whitening a darkened root-canal-treated tooth from the inside; reported high immediate success, with resorption risk and some re-treatment.
lead: Internal (intracoronal) bleaching is a tooth-whitening procedure for root-canal-treated, non-vital teeth, which lose their nerve supply and often darken . The bleaching agent is sealed inside the tooth rather than applied to the outer surface, and is replaced every few weeks until the desired shade is reached; it is most often done on front teeth .

name: Bite reclamation
summary: Rebuilding worn teeth to restore bite height; sources are thin and no trials were found.
lead: Bite reclamation is a term used in cosmetic dentistry for reopening the bite to restore vertical dimension lost through wear, such as from grinding or acid reflux, which can make the lower face look shortened . It is described as part of full-mouth reconstruction, complex work involving many teeth .

name: Wax-up smile mock-up
summary: A model or temporary preview of planned tooth changes, used before veneers; thin sourcing.
lead: A wax-up or mock-up is a diagnostic preview in cosmetic dentistry: dentists build a model of planned tooth changes to guide preparation before veneers are made . It shows how changes in tooth size, shape and proportion will relate to the gums, lips and smile line, and temporaries based on it can test appearance, speech and bite before final work .

name: Surgical orthodontics
summary: Jaw surgery coordinated with braces to correct bite and facial proportions; established medicine with real surgical risks and long recovery.
lead: Surgical orthodontics usually refers to orthodontic treatment combined with orthognathic (corrective jaw) surgery, in which a surgeon cuts, moves and realigns jaw bone to correct bite problems, airway issues and facial imbalance, typically through the mouth and in coordination with an orthodontist . The term is also used for surgically facilitated orthodontics, such as corticotomy, which aims to speed tooth movement .

name: All-on-4
summary: Full-arch fixed teeth on four implants; established dental surgery with reported high survival, but pricey and aimed at tooth loss, not facial change.
lead: All-on-4 is a prosthodontic treatment concept in which a full arch of missing teeth is replaced by a fixed prosthesis supported by four dental implants, the rear two usually tilted so they can be anchored without bone grafting. The prosthesis is typically fitted within about 24 hours of surgery, and "All-on-4" is a trademark of the implant manufacturer Nobel Biocare. It is classed in looksmaxxing culture as a "hardmaxx" dental procedure because it is sometimes pursued to replace failing teeth with a new, uniform smile.

name: Damon self-ligating braces
summary: Passive self-ligating braces sold on low friction and arch expansion; forums rate them top, reviews find mostly mixed benefits.
lead: Damon braces are a line of self-ligating orthodontic brackets, which hold the archwire with a built-in sliding door instead of elastic ties. The Damon SL1 was introduced in 1996 and is classed as a passive self-ligating system. Manufacturers and some orthodontists say the design reduces friction and allows lighter forces, and the system is often marketed for arch expansion without extractions.
claims: Damon braces widen the dental arch better than conventional braces or Invisalign.
Damon braces improve the maxilla or shift the jaw forward.
Damon braces are faster and more comfortable.

name: Teeth whitening pens
summary: Brush-on gel pens for at-home whitening; evidence on pens specifically is lab-only.
lead: Teeth whitening pens are over-the-counter applicator pens that brush a peroxide-based or other whitening gel onto the tooth surface. They are one of several at-home options, alongside strips, trays, rinses and whitening toothpastes. The general Wikipedia article on tooth whitening does not mention pens specifically, so most of what is known comes from small laboratory studies.

name: Peroxycarboxylic (PAP) whitening
summary: Peroxide-free whitening agent (PAP) with one small laser-activated study behind it.
lead: PAP whitening uses phthalimidoperoxycaproic acid, a peroxycarboxylic acid marketed as a non-peroxide-based tooth whitening agent. It is promoted as an alternative to hydrogen peroxide or carbamide peroxide products, which are associated with tooth sensitivity.

name: VITA shade guide
summary: The A1-D4 tooth-colour scale dentists use to describe and track whitening results.
lead: The VITA classical shade guide is a set of tooth-coloured tabs, labelled A1 to D4, used by dentists to describe and match tooth colour. It is arranged by value (lightness) and chroma (colour intensity). In whitening and cosmetic dentistry it serves as a reference scale for stating how light teeth are before and after treatment.

name: Temporal brow lift
summary: Surgical lateral eyebrow lift through temple incisions; documented in surgical series, with surgeon debate over technique.
lead: A temporal (lateral) brow lift is a surgical procedure that raises the outer part of the eyebrow using incisions placed in the hair-bearing temple area. It is one of several brow-lifting approaches that also include coronal, endoscopic, direct and internal (transblepharoplasty) lifts. Patients seek it to lift a drooping brow tail and open the eye area; looksmaxxing communities group it with eye-area surgery.

name: Cheek lift
summary: Surgical repositioning of sagging cheek tissue, studied mainly in ageing faces; looksmaxxing talk about it for young men is largely untested.
lead: A cheek lift, also called a midface lift, is a cosmetic surgical procedure that repositions sagging soft tissue of the cheek, including the malar fat pad, to a higher position on the face. It is performed under the broader heading of facial rejuvenation and is often combined with eyelid surgery or a full facelift .
claims: A cheek lift would make a large difference to how old and attractive a young man looks.
Tanning, cardio and lower body fat can reduce the aged look of the malar area without surgery.
Facial exercises quickly reduce the appearance of malar fat pads.

name: Facial feminization surgery
summary: A set of bone and soft-tissue facial operations developed for transgender women, now eyed by some looksmaxxers for brow, nose and cheek work.
lead: Facial feminization surgery (FFS) is an umbrella term for reconstructive procedures that alter typically masculine facial features toward more typically feminine ones. It is performed mostly for transgender women and other transfeminine people, and includes work on the hairline, forehead and brow ridge, nose, cheeks, lips, chin and jaw, and the thyroid cartilage (Adam's apple) .
claims: FFS techniques such as brow bone shaping and cheek augmentation can remove 'ogre' features and improve harmony in a male face.
Combining FFS with implants would cost more than just getting cheek implants and some brow and nose reshaping.

name: Zygomatic reduction
summary: Surgery to narrow or flatten the cheekbones; popular in Asian aesthetic surgery, with no outcome studies in the wiki's sources.
lead: Zygomatic reduction, also called malarplasty, cheekbone reduction or cheekbone shaving, is a surgical procedure intended to narrow or lower the projection of the cheekbones (the zygomatic bones). The zygomatic bone forms the cheekbone and part of the eye socket wall .
claims: A wide face may come from bone rather than fat, and cheekbone reduction can improve it.
Cheekbone shaving mainly reduces forward projection, not width.
Surgery should only be done when the proportions truly call for it, since it can ruin a harmonious face.

name: Serdev suture
summary: A needle-suture thread lifting method from the suspension-thread family, with thin published evidence on the specific technique.
lead: The Serdev suture is a needle-based suture lifting technique for facial rejuvenation, associated with a surgeon named Serdev, who introduced a polycaproamide suture for facial lifting. It belongs to the broader family of suspension or thread lifts .

name: Facial Autologous Muscular Injection (FAMI)
summary: A fat-grafting variant that places a patient's own fat into facial muscle; almost nothing is published on it specifically.
lead: Facial Autologous Muscular Injection (FAMI), also written as fat autograft muscle injection, is a facial fat-grafting technique in which the patient's own fat is injected into facial muscle for volume restoration and contouring. A 2007 review of fat transfer lists it with lipostructure and facial fat rebalancing as newer concepts aimed at three-dimensional rejuvenation of the whole face .
